name: Buffalo Tom
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Three UMass students got a leg up from J Mascis, found a following in Britain before America, and wrote "Taillights Fade", the song they'll be playing at every show for the rest of their lives.

hero.by: Buffalo Tom live, May 31, 2008. Photo: livepict.com, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Two acoustic guitars in Northampton
eras.text: Buffalo Tom came out of the same western Massachusetts college scene as Dinosaur Jr and Pixies. J Mascis produced their first two records at Fort Apache, and a Dutch label, SST and Beggars Banquet put them out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Buffalo Tom · NHPR · MAGNET · Louder
years.h: Three UMass Amherst students name a band after Buffalo Springfield and their drummer
years.p: [[Bill Janovitz|7563dc86-3dcf-4f3f-9341-4097932376f4]] sings and plays guitar, Chris Colbourn plays bass, and Tom Maginnis drums. The "Tom" is Maginnis.
years.xp: Janovitz and Colbourn started without Maginnis, "as an acoustic duo up in a room of a house in Northampton," Janovitz told NHPR. Colbourn and Maginnis had only recently picked up their instruments, MAGNET reported, and Janovitz had never really sung before the band.

years.h: First show: a folk open night at the Iron Horse, as Buffalo Tom Trio
years.p: The band played its first gig at the Iron Horse in Northampton on a folk open-mic night, which is why the bill said "Trio".

years.src: Wikipedia: Buffalo Tom · Drowned in Sound · MAGNET
years.h: [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] produces the debut and plays lead on "Impossible"
years.p: Recorded at Fort Apache in Boston with Mascis as co-producer, while the band still had day jobs. A Dutch label, Megadisc, issued it first, and SST Records licensed it for America.

years.h: Beggars Banquet signs them in Britain
years.p: Janovitz was thrilled to join the label of [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]] and The Died Pretty. Situation Two released them in the UK, where [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]], Mark Goodier and Everett True backed them early.

years.h: On Birdbrain, J Mascis plays the title-track solo as "Monte Rose"
years.p: Mascis co-produced again with Sean Slade. The CD added a live acoustic cover of [[The Psychedelic Furs|9f930ddf-be2f-4de5-a39f-7ae47305752e]]' "Heaven".

eras.title: A church in the woods, a remix on a private jet
eras.text: Without Mascis, the band cut their third album fast and cheap in a converted church near Woodstock. Then Nevermind came out mid-mix, and their label suddenly wanted more.

years.src: MAGNET · Louder · Wikipedia: Let Me Come Over
years.h: Three days at Dreamland, a converted church near Woodstock
years.p: Sean Slade and Paul Q. Kolderie produced, with basic tracks cut in Hurley, New York, and overdubs at Fort Apache. MAGNET put the budget at $10,000 to $12,000.
years.xp:
Janovitz had discovered the capo, and the songs changed with it. He cited Neil Young, Van Morrison, Bob Dylan and the Stones; with "Mineral" and "Larry" he felt the band had found something new.

"We did all the tracks as fast as we could. The clock was ticking," Maginnis told MAGNET.

years.src: Drowned in Sound · Wikipedia: Let Me Come Over
years.h: Maginnis leaves the studio to see Nirvana in a Boston club
years.p: It was the night before Nevermind came out. He came back saying [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] were the greatest band he'd ever seen.

q: Ron Saint Germain, to Bill Janovitz
years.src: Louder · MAGNET · Wikipedia: Let Me Come Over
years.h: Beggars hires Ron Saint Germain to remix the record
years.p: After Nevermind, the label wanted louder guitars. Saint Germain's remix cost about twice what the album had.
years.xp:
Janovitz had pushed back, and his first reaction to the mixes was shock, "mostly in a bad way." After a day or two he called them undeniable. The band had Saint Germain tone down "some of the stadium rock".

Slade and Kolderie were stung to be sidelined, but Kolderie agreed the remix solved problems they'd had. Their mix of "Frozen Lake" stayed on the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Let Me Come Over · MAGNET
years.h: Let Me Come Over, with a stockman from National Geographic on the cover
years.p: Michael O'Brien's photo of Fred Brown, an Aboriginal Australian stockman, came from the February 1988 issue. Some critics accused the band of "exploiting the black experience".
years.xp: Maginnis told MAGNET the band liked the cover's "off-kilter" feel because it didn't match the music. "Velvet Roof" and "Mineral" were also released as singles.

q: Free Bird is thirteen minutes long, and Taillights is just three and a half.
years.h: Janovitz never saw "Taillights Fade" as the single
years.p: He calls it "pretty dark and depressing". It became the song no Buffalo Tom show goes without.
years.xp: Asked by Classic Rock in 2018 whether it was their "Free Bird", Janovitz laughed and noted the length difference. Kolderie says he knew it would be big the first time he heard it.

years.src: Drowned in Sound · Wikipedia: Let Me Come Over
years.h: Stage divers at the University of London Union
years.p: Britain took to them before America did. The 1992 ULU show had a non-stop stream of fans climbing up and diving off, and they played Reading that summer.
years.xp: The ULU show was released in full on the 25th-anniversary edition of Let Me Come Over in 2017. They played Reading again in 1994.

eras.title: Sodajerk on prime time
eras.text: Nirvana's success opened doors for bands like Buffalo Tom. They charted in Britain, got on MTV, and turned up in a TV drama's club scene.

years.src: Wikipedia: Buffalo Tom · Wikipedia: Big Red Letter Day
years.h: Big Red Letter Day reaches No. 17 in Britain
years.p: It made the UK top 20 in October 1993. "Sodajerk" hit No. 7 on Billboard's alternative chart and ended up in Nike and Pontiac ads.

years.cap: A live review of the Wulfrun Hall show, Wolverhampton, 1993
years.h: "For All to See" on No Alternative
years.p: Buffalo Tom gave a song to the Red Hot Organization's 1993 AIDS benefit album.

yt: "Late at Night" on My So-Called Life
years.h: The band plays "Late at Night" in an episode of My So-Called Life
years.p: The episode "Self-Esteem" puts the band on stage in a club scene. "Sodajerk" was on the show's soundtrack album.

years.cap: Ticket for the Avalon, Boston, September 29, 1995
years.h: The last musical guest on The Jon Stewart Show
years.p: When Jon Stewart's late-night show ended its run, Buffalo Tom played the final episode, with "Summer" from Sleepy Eyed.

years.h: Sleepy Eyed strips the polish back off
years.p: The band wanted a rawer, live sound after Big Red Letter Day. One song's subtitle names Nan Goldin's photo book The Ballad of Sexual Dependency.

eras.title: Keyboards, then a long pause
eras.text: One album on Polydor, one Jam cover that went higher than anything they'd written, and then the band stopped.

years.h: Belly's Tom Gorman tells them to hire a real keyboard player
years.p: The demos leaned on keys, so they tried [[Belly|c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2]]'s Tom Gorman, who pointed them elsewhere. Janovitz found Phil Aiken through a classified ad; [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]] producer David Bianco made the record.

years.h: A Jam cover becomes their biggest UK hit
years.p: Their version of "Going Underground", for a [[The Jam|23228f18-01d5-493e-94ce-cfcde82a8db2]] tribute, shared a double A-side with Liam Gallagher and Steve Cradock's "Carnation". It reached No. 6.

years.cap: Poster for the Australian tour, January 1999
years.src: Drowned in Sound · Wikipedia: Bill Janovitz · Louder Than War
years.h: After Smitten, nine years without an album
years.p: Janovitz cites family and a changing industry. "Yeah, I felt for sure we were done," he told Drowned in Sound.
years.xp: Janovitz made solo records and bar-band albums, including with [[Tanya Donelly|478e2b34-bda3-48c8-81e4-77efac91f3ec]], and became a real-estate agent in Lexington, Massachusetts. Colbourn told Louder Than War he thinks of himself first as a father.

eras.title: Every five years or so
eras.text: The band came back for a hometown show, then for records whenever three people with jobs and families could make them. Meanwhile Janovitz turned into a rock biographer.

years.h: A night at the Paradise in Boston comes out as a live album
years.p: Instant Live 6/10/05 Paradise, Boston, MA caught the first reunion shows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Buffalo Tom · Wikipedia: Three Easy Pieces
years.h: After SXSW, Three Easy Pieces on New West
years.p: Their first album in nine years took two years of on-and-off sessions at Q Division. [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]]'s Clint Conley sings backing vocals.

years.h: Skins, on the band's own Scrawny label
years.p: Announced on Facebook and Twitter, released through The Orchard to good reviews.

years.h: Quiet and Peace ends a seven-year wait
years.p: Self-produced and mixed by John Agnello; Lucy Janovitz sings on "The Only Living Boy in New York". Metacritic averaged the album at 76.

years.h: Janovitz's Leon Russell biography is a New York Times best seller
years.p: After a 33⅓ book on Exile on Main St. and Rocks Off about the Stones, Janovitz wrote on Leon Russell, then on [[The Cars|092b603f-eb4c-4958-b10e-02420de5885b]] in 2025.

years.h: Jump Rope, written out of lockdown notebooks
years.p: Colbourn says he "found" time in the pandemic and went through old song notebooks. The title comes from photographer Mark Cohen's pictures of 1970s Pennsylvania.
